newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest spot power rises amid frigid weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest spot power rises amid frigid weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were trading higher Friday amid frigid temperatures that were expected to last into next week, power brokers and marketers said.

Temperatures in South Dakota were forecast to reach a high of only 0 degrees Fahrenheit on Saturday with a significant wind chill, and longer term forecasts called for much below and below normal temperatures in most of the region through to January 20.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak, non-firm power prices for Monday delivery were discussed at $28.00-32.00 from next day discussion at $22.00-26.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Thursday, the brokers and marketers said.
Spot trade of weekend power in MAPP was said to be very thin.
Off-peak next day non-firm MAPP power was notionally said to be holding steady in the $10.50-12.00 range.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Monday climbed to $28.00-30.50 from next-day discussion at $24.00-26.00 on Thursday.
MAIN weekend spot trade was also reported to be very thin.
MAIN off peak next day power was notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00, the sources said.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Monday were discussed higher at $28.00-30.00 from $25.00-27.00 on Thursday, while weekend peak power was pegged at $18.00-24.00 per MWh.
Peak ECAR power for the five business days of next week was said to have traded at $29.50, although the trade was unconfirmed, from discussion near $26.00 on Thursday, the sources said.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were notionally quoted steady at $13.00-15.00 per MWh.
February ECAR was assessed at $23.50-24.00 from $23.00-25.00 on Thursday, with some traders citing buying interest in the month as it was seen to be good value at current levels.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Monday delivery was talked over a wide range at $29.00-33.00 from $24.00-26.00 for next-day business on Thursday, the sources said.
Weekend SPP peak power was talked near $26.00, the sources said.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP for Monday delivery jumped to $18.00-20.00 from $13.00-15.00 on Thursday, the sources said.
February SPP was said to have risen to $24.00-25.00 from $23.60-24.00 on Thursday, the sources said.

Separately, MidAmerican Energy Co's 675 megawatt Council Bluffs coal fired power unit 3 in Council Bluffs, Iowa, was expected to return to service over the weekend following a repair outage. The unit was shut Jan 8 for a boiler tube leak repair.
Also, the 1,205 megawatt (MW) Perry nuclear power plant in North Perry, Ohio, was increasing electricity production Friday after tripping off line Tuesday due to an electrical problem.
Duquesne Light Co said Friday the 833 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Beaver Valley nuclear power plant in Shippingport, Pa. would resume operation this weekend after it tripped off line Monday.
((--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627))
